    "# Cell-cell communication with CellPhoneDB\n",
    "\n",
    "## Overview\n",
    "\n",
    "Cell-cell communication (CCC) analysis connects ligand-receptor activity with cell-state changes across complex tissues. This tutorial walks through CellPhoneDB-style communication analysis in OmicVerse, starting from the communication `AnnData` and then moving through heatmap, network, summary, and advanced visualization layers.\n",
    "\n",
    "## Citation\n",
    "\n",
    "**Paper**: [Single-cell reconstruction of the early maternal-fetal interface in humans](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-018-0698-6)\n",
    "\n",
    "**Code**: https://github.com/ventolab/CellphoneDB\n",
    "\n",
    "**CellChat Reference**: [Inference and analysis of cell-cell communication using CellChat](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-021-21246-9)\n"
   ]

   "source": [
    "### 1. Heatmap-style views with `ov.pl.ccc_heatmap`\n",
    "\n",
    "This section covers compact aggregated views, dot-matrix views, pathway-focused bubble layouts, and signaling-role summaries. It also includes a quick colormap swap so you can compare the same communication structure under a different palette.\n",
    "\n",
    "Key constraints to keep in mind:\n",
    "\n",
    "- `comparison_adata` is only required for differential plots such as `plot_type='diff_heatmap'`.\n",
    "- `signaling` is required for pathway-specific displays such as `plot_type='pathway_bubble'`.\n",
    "- Aggregated heatmaps should not be filtered with `interaction_use` or `pair_lr_use`.\n",
    "- `plot_type='dot'` works especially well with `display_by='interaction'` when you want to inspect top ligand-receptor pairs.\n",
    "- Role heatmaps summarize pathway roles and are usually shown without `sender_use` or `receiver_use` filters.\n"
   ]
  },

   "source": [
    "### 2. Network views with `ov.pl.ccc_network_plot`\n",
    "\n",
    "`ccc_network_plot` now collects the old aggregate-circle, pathway-circle, outgoing/incoming panel, chord, ligand-receptor chord, gene chord, and differential views behind one public API. This walkthrough now also includes `embedding_network`, `bipartite`, `arrow`, and `sigmoid` examples.\n",
    "\n",
    "Key constraints:\n",
    "\n",
    "- `signaling` is required for `plot_type='pathway'`.\n",
    "- `pair_lr_use` or `interaction_use` is required for `plot_type='lr_chord'`.\n",
    "- `comparison_adata` is required for `plot_type='diff_network'`.\n",
    "- `embedding_network` needs cell-type coordinates and optional background embedding points; here we reuse the original UMAP stored in `adata`.\n",
    "- `bipartite` can be focused with `ligand` and `receptor` filters.\n",
    "- `arrow` and `sigmoid` are most useful with `display_by='interaction'` when you want to show the sender -> ligand-receptor -> receiver flow.\n"
   ]
  },
